summary:
I've been building a Japanese-learning app for myself, and this stretch went mostly into the art pipeline rather than the app. Cards get illustrated through two different image backends, and for weeks one of them was quietly ignoring the style prompt and every content restriction I'd written — no negative prompts reaching the request at all. It looked like the model just refusing to behave, and I spent real time arguing with prompts before I actually read the function sending the request and found the wiring only applied those on one code path. Related but separate: a thumbnail crop that looked fine on my desktop was showing about a third of the image on a phone, from the same CSS — a `cover` crop scales with viewport width, so the narrowest screen produces the widest crop. Fixed both by going back to the actual code path instead of re-rolling the output and hoping.

On the Hermes-Agent side — the personal automation agent I run at home — I chased down a Slack integration that had been silently dead for a week: 180,000-plus errors in the log, zero messages delivered, and nothing paged because a healthy connection logs nothing at all, so a naive health check that watches for success lines can't tell dead from quiet. Had to invert it — alert on the error signature instead, with a cooldown so a restart doesn't fire the same alert on a loop. Same agent had a separate bug where an internal memory tool's error messages described what was wrong but never what to do next, so the model would retry the same failing call for minutes at a time. Rewriting the error text to name the actual next step fixed more of that behavior than any amount of prompt tuning did.

On BudgetTracker, I built out a set of read-only MCP tools so an LLM can answer real questions about spending data directly against Postgres — account balances, daily totals, a 14-day run-rate forecast — instead of summarizing a CSV export. The interesting part was tightening the auth handshake between the two services and catching a couple of date-handling bugs in the SQL that only showed up once real queries started hitting it.

A pattern across all three: most of what looked like "the model is being difficult" turned out to be a wiring bug or a misleading error message a few layers down, and the fix was almost always to read the actual code path rather than iterate on the prompt.

highlights.oneLiner: Japanese-learning app: fixed a broken image-style pipeline and a mobile crop bug
Chased a silently dead Slack integration and a memory-tool error that stalled retries
Built read-only MCP tools so an LLM can query spending data directly against Postgres
